newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar ends up on good demand, limited supply.
newsitem.headline: India sugar ends up on good demand, limited supply.

text.p: Indian sugar prices extended gains on Friday on sustained consumer buying, dealers said.
Strong consumer demand pushed prices up while limited supplies from mills kept offerings at a low level, they said.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 rose 5 rupees to 1,390/1,425 and M-30 climbed to 1,440/1,505 rupees from 1,420/1,487 rupees, dealers said.

Sugar mill delivery lost ground and slid to 1,320/1,330 rupees per quintal from 1,340/1,360 rupees on increased supply from mills on market reports of an increase in the free sale quota for May, one trader said.

"Free sale quota for May is 750,000 tonnes while it was 700,000 tonnes for last month," he said. "Market talk is the government may release additional quota of 75,000/100,000 tonnes for May to check the buoyancy in prices."
